Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.
  • Industry observers note that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Industry observers note that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

In a recent development, remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it swiftly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

It has been revealed that both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It was typical of Brighton that one of their upcoming signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another fresh signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

Recent findings suggest that this was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

Industry observers note that “The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “massive lesson” for his players.

It has been revealed that “There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

In a recent development, “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

It has been revealed that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a substantial lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

According to recent reports, “Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta remarked. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, noted. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

According to recent reports, two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

As half-time approaches, Arsenal have mustered just one shot on goal worth 0.03 expected goals. When they have moved the ball beyond Brighton’s press, they have not done anywhere near enough with it.

This fixture last season was especially bad-tempered, with the Brighton fans (and manager) repeatedly accusing Arsenal of time-wasting. The bad blood is adding to the intensity of the occasion.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the latest buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

We are getting to the stage where we really need to start asking questions about Tino Livramento’s injury record.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring complications.

Injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

According to recent reports, elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although the EFL Championship season is only 15 games old, former striker Kevin Phillips has outlined his current worries for three sides in the division at this moment in time.

The second tier of English football is renowned for pulling up plenty of surprises throughout almost every 46-game season, and no doubt many more are lying in wait in the coming months.

At present, the top end of the Championship is extremely congested, with only eight points separating the 12 sides occupying places in the divison's top-half, with one of Phillips' many former sides, Birmingham City, currently leading the way on goal difference.

However, some are presently at risk of cutting themselves adrift when it comes to an unwanted relegation to League One, and it is fair to say that the one-time experienced forward, who is now a regular fixture on our television screens, has his concerns over multiple clubs in stated situation.

Phillips, 53, enjoyed an esteemed playing career in both the Premier League and Championship, which included promotions from the division with all of Birmingham, Crystal Palace, Leicester City, Sunderland and West Bromwich Albion.

Netting 134 of his career goals at second tier level, the former striker knows exactly what it takes to be successful in the division both collectively and individually, as well as seeing the other side of the game at first-hand through an array of coaching and managerial roles.

Speaking to Football League World via Best Betting Sites, Phillips explained his worries over three clubs, two of which he has affiliations with in the form of Watford and Derby County.

"Well, there are a few, to be fair. A couple of my old teams I used to play for, and one I coached at," he stated. "The team I'm most worried about, and the team where they shouldn't be, they should be a lot higher and doing better things, is Watford. I speak about them quite a lot.

In a recent development, "I never know what to expect from them on and off the pitch, but history should suggest that they should be doing a lot better than what they're doing. So I fear for my old club. They've been in and around the relegation zone, avoided relegation, and I really fear for them this season," Phillips added.

"They might slip through. I really hope they don't, and I hope they find a bit of form, but I fear for them.

Phillips then discussed the situation at Burnley, with the Clarets in danger of becoming the third club in as many seasons to suffer successive relegations from the Premier League to League One.

According to recent reports, "And of course Burnley as well, from where they've been to where they are now. The season they're having for such a big club, in the Premier League not so long ago, to be where they are now, having only won one game in the Championship," the former striker continued.

"It's been really disappointing, so I'm worried for them. And I think Derby as well. I hope they pick up form. So two of my old clubs are in there, but Watford and Burnley for sure.".

Phillips broke through the Watford ranks, meaning it is no real surprise he has concerns over the Hornets at present given his attachment to the club.

Alessio Dionisi was drafted in as the 24th head coach of Gino Pozzo's ownership in June on a two-year contract, but after making an encouraging start 2-1 victory against high-flying Southampton on the opening day, it was downhill from there for the Italian.

Winning three games since and given the ownership consortium's reputation for firing-and-hiring saw intense speculation over another sacking come to the fore last month, and after Saturday's 4-0 loss to Sheffield United at Bramall Lane, Dionisi was sacked after just 18 matches in charge.

Many would also agree with Phillips' concerns over Burnley and Derby right now, with the two sides making up the bottom three alongside Preston North End after 16 games.

The Clarets have only defeated Watford so far this term, and in recent weeks, the vulnerability of the squad at Turf Moor has been laid bare for all to see.

Nicky Hayen's tenure lasted just 14 games, with his final two outings seeing Burnley surrender leads against Wolves and Lincoln City, whilst Fabio Celestini's tenure has got off to a winless start.

The Swiss head coach admitted before the international break that his fresh chargers are certainly in a dogfight to preserve their Championship status after his side gave up a comfortable 4-1 lead away to Cardiff City to lose 5-4, with Kyle Walker issuing a similar stance after Sunday's compelling 2-2 draw with Blackburn Rovers in the East Lancashire derby.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his newly introduced squad, but its release quickly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage demonstrated players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from fresh head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its latest head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

“Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

Industry observers note that manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a substantial reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in important matches.

“A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of big trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in big games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

Sources indicate that pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

Recent findings suggest that the Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

Mauricio Pochettino has made it clear he wants to be involved in Manchester United’s major squad decisions, while also addressing questions surrounding captain Bruno Fernandes ahead of his first game against Liverpool.

The new Manchester United head coach explained that he wants to have a voice in decisions that shape the squad.

“Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino said in his first Manchester United press conference.

“It depends on the structure, it depends on the communication, the relationships, you know, with all the areas.”.

Mauricio Pochettino highlighted his responsibilities are clear about who he selects and plays in games.].

“I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I’m going to pick the team, I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad.”.

Pochettino was also asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The Argentine was really keen about the squad’s commitment, dodging the blame on Fernandes and describing Fernandes as a key figure in the dressing room.

“The commitment from all the players was amazing from day one,” he said.

“Bruno is our captain and a very crucial player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.”.

Pochettino revealed that he had already spent time speaking with the players to understand their situation both on and off the pitch.

“Yesterday we spent three hours chatting to the players in my office and maybe I missed the injured players.”.

Pochettino admitted the first few days at United had been extremely busy as he tried to get up to speed before his first match.

He is excited by the opportunity but knows there is little time to prepare for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

“It’s a happy time but at the same time, so busy,” he explained.

“It’s been about adapting in the last few days, and it’s a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool in the game on Sunday.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg admitted that he "couldn't understand" how enormous the interest surrounding a football club in a specific town or city was before he came over to coach Boro last year.

The Swedish boss celebrated one year at the Riverside on Tuesday, and in that time, Middlesbrough have been transformed and look certain to be playing Premier League football in the near future.

Boro were inside the top two when Hellberg was hired, following the shock departure of Rob Edwards, but the brand of football he has instilled in the club has been thoroughly entertaining, both for fans of the club and neutrals alike.

Middlesbrough have a proud fanbase, and after years of Championship obscurity, they look to be on the rise again, and the energy surrounding the club from the fanbase is something that Hellberg has been surprised by during his first year on Teesside.

According to recent reports, kim Hellberg has seemed destined to coach in England ever since he started managing in Sweden a decade ago. But, as is often the case with foreign coaches, he was taken aback by the swell of support which surrounds football in this country.

It's tribalistic at times, and the fact that smaller cities and towns can have such a loyal, large following is always something that first-time coaches in this country take as a surprise. Hellberg is no different.

What's been your favourite moment from Kim Hellberg's first year in charge at Middlesbrough, Boro fans? Let us know in the comments.

It has been revealed that to celebrate one year in charge at the Riverside, Middlesbrough ran a Q&A with their head coach, with him answering questions from fans. One such query regarded what has surprised him the most about Boro.

"I know football was everything here, but the biggest surprise for me was the enormous interest and energy around the football club," he mentioned.

"How everyone feels like they care about Middlesbrough and live through that, how important football is wherever you go, wherever you are, football is everything here. I think I knew some bits were like that, but I couldn't understand how big it was.".

Kim Hellberg will likely be referencing how most English clubs have such a passionate fanbase that lives through the team, but in Middlesbrough especially, that's evident.

Boro are a one-club town. No other professional team is in the Middlesbrough area, with the closest professional club being Hartlepool United, 13 miles away. Even then, those in Hartlepool count themselves more in County Durham, rather than Teesside.

Either way, it's a proud following at Boro, and has been for years. Their time in the Premier League grew that, but even in the past few years, attendances at the Riverside have hovered around the 25,000 mark in the Championship.

All you have to do is look at the numbers over the past year to know that Kim Hellberg is bringing back some of the supporter base who may have become a little disassociated with the club as they stagnated in the second tier, though.

Recent findings suggest that boro's lowest Saturday attendance this season was against Cardiff City, at 28,991. Their average attendance in the entirety of last season was 27,622, and the year before, in Michael Carrick's final term, it was 25,416.

Over 3,000 more fans are coming to watch this Middlesbrough team under Hellberg than they were in the final moments of the Carrick reign, which shows how much bigger an already massive support has been under Hellberg.

Hellberg went on to say that his dream as Boro boss was to bring the club back to the Premier League, which he hopes to do this season.

Middlesbrough presently sit atop the Championship table, and look good value for it, too. What's arguably more scary, though, is that they seem to still have a higher gear that they can reach, and if they can find it, they may win this league at a canter.

Then, the Swedish boss may end up being taken further aback by the extra support which will come at the top level. Boro are a club that has been starved of Premier League football, with this being the 17th of the last 18 seasons they've spent in the Championship.

You get the feeling, though, that if Hellberg can get this side into the top flight, they'll stand a greater chance of staying there than they did under Aitor Karanka a decade ago.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

Sources indicate that the figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

Pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

United’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

In a recent development, the former MK Dons, Swansea City, Southampton, and Rangers boss has now taken charge of five clubs, with Leicester representing his latest challenge. After a difficult start, he is beginning to show why the Foxes appointed him.

Martin's appointment at Leicester was always going to divide opinion, particularly after his disastrous 123-day spell at Rangers, where he won just five of his 17 matches before being dismissed.

He then endured a difficult start in the East Midlands, winning two and losing three of his first eight league fixtures. The pressure was considerable given Leicester's expectation of bouncing straight back to the Championship, with another season in League One representing a disaster for a club of their stature.

It has been revealed that simon Jordan was among those questioning Martin's position at Leicester, with things looking particularly bleak after the 3-1 defeat to Peterborough United and former Leicester player Robbie Savage. The warning was there that he would be sacked unless results improved.

It has been revealed that however, the Foxes have since won four of their next six league games, including that outstanding Huddersfield victory. Rangers supporters and some of the divisive coach’s other critics could be eating their words.

It has been revealed that they have always piled on Martin for last season, with neither they nor Jordan perhaps enjoying seeing him turn things around. Leicester are looking considerably more positive, easy on the eye, and results are following.

Martin's Southampton side also took time to get going, suffering four consecutive defeats early in his first season before eventually embarking on a remarkable 25-match unbeaten run.

George Elek, an EFL expert and Not The Top 20 podcast pundit, has argued that Martin's reputation has become a footballing culture war, with his failures often attracting considerably more attention than his achievements.

In a recent development, will Russell Martin return Leicester to the Championship at the first time of asking? Comment below!

In further replies on X (formerly Twitter), Elek added: "Tough ask to expect him to come on board a sinking ship and turn it around straight away. League position at this stage is pretty meaningless, they’re clearly playing well now. Why do you think chucking money at it will solve the clear rot that had set in? His playing style is extreme. Is he not entitled to have some time to implement it?".

There is a reasonable argument that Leicester simply needed to give him time to implement his ideas, particularly given the scale of the rebuilding job. The Foxes could now be ready to climb the table rapidly and become genuine automatic promotion contenders rather than simply hoping to sneak into the play-offs.

Recent findings suggest that there is, however, a cautionary tale from Martin's Southampton tenure. Despite that extraordinary unbeaten run, Saints eventually fizzled out during the closing stages of the 2023/24 campaign, losing three games in one damaging April week and missing out on automatic promotion.

Recent findings suggest that they entered the play-offs with questions surrounding their form, although they ultimately overcame Leeds at Wembley. Leicester would happily take that outcome, but should be wary of allowing their standards to drop once the initial momentum arrives.

Martin has the midfield quality to dominate League One for the foreseeable future, with John Lundstram, Sammy Braybrooke, Will Smallbone, and Louis Page offering an excellent blend of technical ability, energy and composure.

That engine room could become the foundation of a serious promotion challenge from this point forth. Rangers fans and Jordan would not enjoy that turnaround, should it come to fruition.

Michael Olise has moved from former Chelsea academy footnote to genuine Ballon d’Or conversation piece.

The point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Sources indicate that olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

Industry observers note that the market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

Recent findings suggest that olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

Sources indicate that this is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any new wide signing.

ReadChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

He is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

  • With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.
  • Industry observers note that united travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

Industry observers note that united travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Industry observers note that fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Recent findings suggest that sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

In a recent development, diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that with a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Industry observers note that juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Industry observers note that liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

It has been revealed that those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EFL pundits Callum Fowler and Jimmy Smith have issued a warning to the Plymouth Argyle hierarchy after Tom Cleverley's side were defeated 2-0 by Peterborough United at Home Park without the attacking quality of Canadian forward, Bim Pepple.

Argyle's positive start to the League One season has hit stumbling block, with the home defeat to Robbie Savage's side following a heavy 3-0 defeat to Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough.

Harry Leonard's goal put the seal on things for Posh after his namesake, Harry Ashfield, opened the scoring midway through the first period.

Other results meant the Green Army dropped to seventh in the table, having taken 23 points from their opening 16 matches.

However, the growing concern surrounding Cleverley's men is their transfer strategy and lack of potential strength-in-depth, with the former Manchester United and England midfielder opting for a front two of Will Evans and Caleb Watts, with Pepple absent for just a third time this campaign.

Pepple moved to Home Park from Luton Town last summer in a deal which could rise as high as £600k, with the former Chesterfield loanee netting 16 times in just 35 League One appearances for the Pilgrims last term as Cleverley's men narrowly missed out on the play-offs.

The 23-year-old has scored five times so far this term, but was sidelined before the defeat to Sheffield Wednesday with a muscular concern.

Regardless, Cleverley backed his fellow attackers to step up to the plate and provide goals, but with blanks fired in the past 180 minutes' worth of action, questions have arisen on this particular front.

Pepple was one half of Argyle's formidable attacking duo last season, with Lorent Tolaj finding the net 21 times in his 35 appearances for the club, before the Swiss youth international was sold to Bristol City in a £4m deal.

Plymouth then sought to replace the 25-year-old with Evans, who is yet to replicate his prior Mansfield Town exploits after a £400,000 agreement, having netted just three times whilst starting in all of his latest employers' 16 league encounters.

Discussing a potential overreliance on Pepple, Fowler mentioned on the Pyramid podcast: "They've got some good players, but they're screaming out for a 'proper' forward.

According to recent reports, "Pepple didn't play in this (game). He's not there.

"So, from what were your starting strikers last season in Tolaj and Pepple, both brilliant for this level. They've got Evans and Watts," he added.

"That's where your problem is, it's a lack of quality," Fowler claimed.

According to recent reports, plymouth fans, do you agree with this viewpoint of your club's attacking department? Comment below!

"I do think Plymouth's owners are trying to be as sustainable as possible.

"If you continue to sell your best players and try and replace them with a cheap option, you will just go down and down and down.

Sources indicate that "Plymouth aren't completely out of this run-in. Obviously, it depends on how long Pepple's out for, but it is a bit concerning losing 2-0 at home to Peterborough.".

The concerns raised by Fowler and Smith are particularly valid, both in the short and long-term, as it remains to be seen when Pepple returns from injury, as well as where he is playing his football in the coming months.

Several Championship sides have been credited with interest in his services, as well as Scottish Premiership side, Celtic, within the past 12 months, and it would be no surprise if the forward wanted to test himself regularly at second tier level after just 13 prior appearances.

With Evans and Watts only scoring five between them so far this season, it is apparent that Argyle may need to reinvest further in January if they are to keep pace with the many promotion hopefuls right now in League One, as only nine points separate Huddersfield Town in second and 13th-placed Mansfield right now.

#187058. Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1094 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned.
  • And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions, with a belligerence of their own, ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. Their mistake was in thinking it was dead.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.

Industry observers note that by this point, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal were 1-0 in front. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

Sources indicate that ‘We were exceptional in the first half,’ he later said. ‘We have won matches playing much worse than we did here. The intensity, the aggression – we should have been 3-0 or 4-0 up. But right from the start of the second half, we weren’t at the races. We lost duels, gave the ball away and gave them belief.’.

Industry observers note that arteta had Noni Madueke to thank for rescuing the point. The winger was his best player throughout and, had he earlier shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

So dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more bloodthirst when on top.

Industry observers note that arteta, you feel, gets more of a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday.

‘The second half was pure belief, pure conviction, pure trust in the team-mate,’ mentioned Jaissle, under increased scrutiny amid the presence of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan.

It has been revealed that ‘There were so many ball-wins with a vertical approach and causing them problems. This is the Newcastle DNA.’.

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes - booed after each of his 36, ineffectual touches - was hooked in the 70th minute, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

According to recent reports, the league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya that requires an MRI scan.

The goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his shoulder, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders.

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained.

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured.

If Newcastle were to beat Arsenal, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast.

At least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as the half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence.

In a recent development, come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to.

Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90).

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret.

The goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine.

Sources indicate that the punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless. Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red.

So, it was as if two sides had swapped shirts after the break. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits.

Recent findings suggest that suddenly, they were able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive, they drew level just four minutes after the restart.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss.

The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend - Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

'We needed players with more energy and physicality,’ said Jaissle, explaining his half-time changes.

‘The tactics did not change, it was purely the front footed behaviour. Throw away the doubts, then you saw what is possible. We had Arsenal shaking. I hope we can carry on this feeling.’.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle looked the most likely winners until Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. Still, the hosts came back for more.

Arsenal had arrived intent on silencing St James’. In the end, they were grateful for the sound of the full-time whistle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

In a recent development, pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the new head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

According to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

It has been revealed that the Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

In a recent development, dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

According to recent reports, the defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical plan was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

In a recent development, united return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the complications exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

According to recent reports, pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

In a recent development, for Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

Chelsea Could Claim Share of £164m Compensation

📅 28 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readchelsea

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years.
  • Sources indicate that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision.
  • Sources indicate that the Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Sources indicate that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

Sources indicate that the Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

It has been revealed that according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

In a recent development, that statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

According to recent reports, data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

It has been revealed that within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

In a recent development, prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a big boost. It could help fund latest signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

It has been revealed that chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has criticised the players’ performance and questioned supporters applauding them after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, insisting the early red card was no excuse for the manner of the loss.
  • Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge unravelled when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes at Anfield.
  • Speaking on Sky Sports, Keane challenged the suggestion that United’s performance was understandable because they had played most of the match with 10 men.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has criticised the players’ performance and questioned supporters applauding them after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, insisting the early red card was no excuse for the manner of the loss.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge unravelled when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes at Anfield. Liverpool scored twice inside 13 minutes and added two more goals after the break, leaving United 19th in the Premier League.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Keane challenged the suggestion that United’s performance was understandable because they had played most of the match with 10 men.

“Fans are applauding. Applauding what?” he asked, before describing the performance as “rubbish”.

Keane argued that United should have shown greater fight and quality, claiming Liverpool could have scored eight or nine goals. He also questioned why responsibility for the club’s problems so often fell on managers, owners and executives rather than the players themselves.

In a recent development, some travelling supporters applauded the team after the final whistle, potentially recognising the difficulty of playing more than 80 minutes with a numerical disadvantage. Keane, however, viewed the reaction as evidence of declining expectations.

Keane also challenged fellow former United captain Gary Neville, who had suggested the early dismissal made the result more understandable. Neville was far from satisfied with United’s performance, though, and separately accused the club’s hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen the defence.

The disagreement reflected two concerns surrounding United: the players’ response to adversity and the quality of the squad available to Pochettino. Liverpool’s goals came from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the hosts creating numerous further opportunities.

Pochettino defended his players’ commitment afterwards and questioned Yoro’s dismissal, arguing that Alexander Isak had not established control of the ball when the defender challenged him. United have taken just eight points from 11 Premier League matches, leaving their newly introduced manager with little time to improve results. They travel to Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action.

Keane’s criticism adds to the scrutiny surrounding the squad following another heavy defeat to their fiercest rivals. For Pochettino, the immediate challenge is to improve defensive organisation while restoring confidence in a side struggling near the bottom of the table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

Recent findings suggest that according to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

Sources indicate that “To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he said, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher said.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that united host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Recent findings suggest that koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

“There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”.

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I remarked it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of important players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”.

Sources indicate that chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

According to recent reports, koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

Industry observers note that for now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

Recent findings suggest that before the injury forced him out, Xabi Alonso had made his admiration for Joao Pedro clear. The Chelsea manager ranked the forward among the Premier League’s elite strikers, alongside Manchester City’s Erling Haaland.

“So I would rate him that way. He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, and to be a nominee for not just this month but more months. I am not surprised, but really happy with the kind of player that we have here with João.”.

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Alonso must lean again on the depth built into his squad.

His approach to rotation, part of the squad management this season, faces another test while his in-form forward is unavailable.

Sources indicate that manchester City have been found guilty of 114 financial charges, the Premier League has confirmed. The verdict follows an eight-week hearing that opened almost two years ago. It closes one of the most significant disciplinary cases in the competition’s history.

Recent findings suggest that former head coach Pep Guardiola has already broken his silence. Reaction to the Pep Guardiola Man City charges verdict is spreading fast across the division, with Chelsea among the clubs watching closely.

Guardiola joined Manchester City in 2016 and turned them into the dominant force in English football. He left his post earlier this summer, with the club having already worked through aims to replace Pep Guardiola at City.

His exit means he holds no formal role at the Etihad. Yet he moved promptly to make his loyalty clear once the ruling landed. According to the football.london report that first carried his statement, Guardiola posted directly to his supporters.

“I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman [Khaldoon Al Mubarak], Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”.

Industry observers note that manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has confirmed that the club intends to appeal the verdict. The statement from Guardiola comes to City’s defence despite him leaving the role this summer. He is still viewed as the man who built this era of success, even though he no longer sits in the dugout at the Etihad.

It has been revealed that the Pep Guardiola Man City charges case matters just as much to Chelsea as it does to Manchester City themselves. Chelsea, along with Arsenal and Tottenham, are among the Premier League clubs directly affected by the outcome. Every point City may have gained through breaches has a knock on effect further down the table.

Most top flight clubs including Chelsea are now pushing for City to face relegation as a consequence of the verdict. Some are reported to be weighing up legal action of their own. Guardiola has spoken about Chelsea before, including Guardiola’s previous comments on Chelsea. This latest statement fits a pattern of public backing for Manchester City, despite the criticism now directed at the club.

Sources indicate that for Chelsea supporters, the case is not just about points on a table. It touches on the integrity of seasons they competed in directly. That is why so many rivals are refusing to let the matter rest with a guilty verdict alone.

Industry observers note that manchester City’s appeal process is now the next stage in a case that has already run for nearly two years. Ferran Soriano has made clear the club will contest the findings. No date has been confirmed for when that appeal will be heard.

Until then, no points deductions, penalties or changes to past titles have been confirmed by the Premier League. Chelsea and their rivals will be watching the appeal timeline just as closely as they watched the original hearing. The final outcome could still be a long way off.

Cesc Fabregas is looking at adding another attacking option after striker Moise Kean suffered another injury setback that is expected to keep him out for several months.

Fabregas confirmed that Kean had aggravated an existing during training last week expected to keep him out for months.

The Italy international has been struggling with a recurring tibia concern and has not featured since representing his country during the September-October international break.

Kean’s extended absence has forced Como to consider other options, with Zirkzee now among the players being monitored ahead of the winter transfer window.

In a recent development, zirkzee has a frustrating time of his own at Manchester United since arriving from Bologna in 2024 for an initial €42.5 million. The forward has failed to get into the team under Michael Carrick and hasn’t started a game so far into the current season.

With Mauricio Pochettino arriving at United, things are uncertain but given his minutes he would fancy a move back to Serie A, if given a chance. Como are emerging as potential suitors for the Netherlands international.

Industry observers note that zirkzee is yet to start a competitive game for United during the 2026-27 campaign. He has made 11 substitute appearances across the Premier League, Champions League and EFL Cup but has struggled to convince the coaching staff that he deserves a regular place.

His situation was even more difficult under former manager Michael Carrick, with the Dutchman appearing to have little chance of breaking into the starting XI.

However, the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino has brought some uncertainty over his future. The upcoming head coach will have his own assessment of the squad, and it remains to be seen whether Zirkzee features in his intends.

Como have shown interest in the striker, but there have been no formal negotiations between the clubs at this stage.

If the situation doesn’t change, January could he a chance for Zirkzee to get his move back to Serie A where he excelled. Much will depend on Pochettino’s looks and whether Como decide to turn their interest into a concrete approach.
