💡 Key Takeaways
  • A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.
  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Sources indicate that lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil stated after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

Sources indicate that west Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

Recent findings suggest that MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

Industry observers note that RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs.

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”.

Industry observers note that seats are filling up rapidly with barely 10 minutes before kick-off, with the away end a notable exception. The home fans are making their own presence felt as The Jam’s A Town Called Malice and The Clash’s London Calling blare out over the public-address system.

Kevin Nolan, West Ham’s captain, was sent off early but his team-mates defied the odds to win 2-1 thanks to goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid either side of a stunning Liam Trotter strike.

Sources indicate that this rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

In a recent development, “There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

Industry observers note that “It really is about the hooligan era,” says a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

Sources indicate that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at Upcoming Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Sources indicate that mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Recent findings suggest that just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

On potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

Recent findings suggest that riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

According to recent reports, the game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

It has been revealed that acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Sources indicate that both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Sources indicate that much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.
  • The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.
  • Industry observers note that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Industry observers note that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino said.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

In a recent development, “But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

It has been revealed that the FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

Industry observers note that in Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Sources indicate that yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park.

Frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’.

Frick demonstrates his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen.

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

The striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to rapidly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

For the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

If Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game.

Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

His next contribution defied belief.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall highlighted him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann stated: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really major, big chances, and we don't take them.

‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’.

Industry observers note that camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

Recent findings suggest that “Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. According to recent reports, “I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. “It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”.

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

Recent findings suggest that “That is the biggest mistake of the major clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term strategy. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

According to recent reports, “Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your strategy. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”.

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”.

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

Recent findings suggest that “I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.
  • Recent findings suggest that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Recent findings suggest that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

Industry observers note that white left the England World Cup camp in November 2022, returning home due to personal reasons. The FA confirmed that White will not return to the squad and asked that his privacy be respected.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

This meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

When White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

He has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss noted after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

The bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

The main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

It has been revealed that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Recent findings suggest that winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

In a recent development, the changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not presently planning to recruit a replacement.

Industry News: West Ham’s Answer Was There All Along – So Why Ignore It?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.
  • At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down.
  • In a recent development, what’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.

At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down. It’s called Jarrod Bowen, and I’m not entirely sure I’ve ever seen our captain play wider than he did at the London Stadium yesterday.

In a recent development, what’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City. On that occasion, Parker was effectively handed a blueprint for getting the best out of West Ham’s most crucial player, yet we’ve barely seen it since.

During that extraordinary second-half comeback against Cardiff, Bowen was given a certain amount of freedom, perhaps encouraged by Parker or maybe he just took it upon himself to drift into the middle of the pitch and cause havoc.

Whatever the reason, he had a hand in all three West Ham goals, and the difference was remarkable.

For the first, he drifted into what might be regarded as the number 10 position and chipped a lovely ball over the Cardiff back line for Divine Mukasa to finish.

It has been revealed that the second was similar, with Bowen again creating the opening from a central position. His pass found Joël Piroe, whose flick released Arne Engels to score.

The third goal saw Bowen back in his more familiar position on the right-hand side, where he supplied a wonderful inswinging cross for Max Kilman to equalise.

Jarrod Bowen was given license to roam against Cardiff.

Recent findings suggest that but that only went to show quite how much freedom Bowen had. In essence, he was everywhere.

As a blueprint, Scott Parker couldn’t have been given a better gift on his first day in charge than discovering that West Ham’s best player could operate with devastating effect from a free role.

Indeed, I was so encouraged by what I saw that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker must restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon following the defeat at Blackburn.

Because for a brief period against Cardiff, it looked as though we’d stumbled upon something rather special.

Therefore, I was a little underwhelmed that we didn’t see it repeated against Blackburn and very worried when we probably saw our captain more straightjacketed than ever against Preston North End.

If I could offer Parker one piece of encouragement or advice, it would be to get the best out of Bowen.

I’m quite sure our upcoming head coach will improve the defence, and I think we saw signs of that yesterday, albeit against the league’s worst team.

But it can’t come at the expense of shackling our best player, who potentially could only be here for a few more months.

As I argued in my assessment of the Preston draw, West Ham had plenty of possession, shots and territory, but very little magic.

And that’s the really bloody annoying part. We have a player who can provide exactly that, but we’re asking him to operate in a way which makes life considerably easier for the opposition.

Recent findings suggest that I know one thing. If I was head coach of an opposition Championship team and I saw Jarrod Bowen shackled to the right wing, I’d breathe a huge sigh of relief.

Because West Ham get one shot at this.

According to recent reports, if we don’t succeed in getting promotion, Bowen could leave for a pittance of £15m. That’s the release clause in the revised contract he agreed following relegation.

We do know that Bowen flew to Prague to meet Daniel Křetínský before pledging to remain at West Ham for another season, as he explained in his interview with Sky Sports.

And I’m now very fearful that we are going to waste what should really be something of a cheat code for the division.

Recent findings suggest that bowen is comfortably our best attacking player, and we’ve already seen how devastating he can be when allowed to roam. Yet rather than building upon that discovery, Parker appears to have returned him to a position where he’s easier to mark and less able to influence the game.

I wish it weren’t so, but I’ve now come to the conclusion that the second half against Cardiff was a pure accident rather than a window into what we could begin to see from Scott Parker as he got his teeth into the West Ham job.

But decisions like that could well make the difference between automatic promotion and a play-off place, if we’re lucky.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

It has been revealed that england will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

Breaking: Fresh system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (951 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.
  • Sources indicate that there were, however, some noticeable improvements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

Sources indicate that there were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent strategy for creating chances.

But the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a fresh manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace.

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel problems in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

Sources indicate that newly introduced boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the major positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’.

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Recent findings suggest that coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

It has been revealed that palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat.

Anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

That is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant problem.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition quickly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni.

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that the Coventry boss remarked: ‘It’s a big win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s important to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

In a recent development, frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

It has been revealed that arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

In a recent development, london City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

The Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta swiftly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

Recent findings suggest that his physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a newly introduced attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

The reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

Sources indicate that only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, debuted a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

Industry observers note that it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

In a recent development, suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

It has been revealed that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi noted: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

Industry observers note that that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he stated: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Sources indicate that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Sources indicate that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Recent findings suggest that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery mentioned. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Reversing Nuno’s decision to cast out Edson Alvarez from the senior team proved a massive success.. Who knew.

Yesterday’s re-integration of ‘El Machin’ into the starting line up was his first league appearance in a West Ham shirt since May 2025.

“He brought every bit of what we needed. It’s a young team, and his experience today in terms of organising and his general presence on the pitch was very, very good for us for large aspects.

Industry observers note that “It was a big ask and I knew that going into the game, he hasn’t played at all this year and probably hasn’t had a lot of training in and around the first team. The Mexican clearly cares: He was in tears before kick off, so tough has his time in the football wilderness been.

It has been revealed that having been such a critic of him during his card-strewn Lopetegui era, credit where it is due. Edson Alvarez was, indeed, excellent yesterday and it is a testimony to his professionalism that he played a full ninety after not playing competitive football since August.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Preston North End, the bottom side in the Championship, arrived in east London yesterday unaffected by the occasion and kept West Ham at bay for an hour until Dinos Mavropanos headed equaliser restored parity and saved Scott Parker’s blushes.

Two weeks’ work during the international break had accounted for very little as Preston withstood everything the Hammers and their almost 60,000 fans had to throw at their lowly opponents.

And therein lies the problem. Having surrendered the small, intimidating, sometimes downright hostile atmosphere of Upton Park back in 2016, the distance from the pitch and the wide open spaces of the Olympic Stadium are about as intimidating as a day out at London Zoo for our opponents and their fans who continue to pour scorn on the venue.

It just doesn’t strike fear into opponents as it should. Even when we score.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium – as our opponents are finding out.

Preston fan Tm Mercer, writing in the Lancashire Evening Post, makes it abundantly clear that there was no noticeable crowd reaction to lift the home side, as there should have been once Mavropanos restored parity:.

“Aside from play-off finals, I’m pretty certain it is the first time I’ve been in a stadium for a league match with 60,000-plus through the gate.

In a recent development, yet, when they equalised, it did not feel like the roar of that many people in such a cavernous ground. Give me somewhere like Gigg Lane, stood in their paddock pitch side, any day!”.

For the uninitiated, Gigg Lane is the home of Bury FC with a capacity of around…..12,000.

According to recent reports, nobody is suggesting the Hammers fans were silent. The cursèd accoustics from the soulless bowl and sheer distance from the pitch play right into opponents’ hands. And, ten years after moving in, it’s going to take a lot more than some safe standing and a couple of family zones to fix it.

  • Separated by just two points in the battle for top-eight places in the Championship table, Sheffield United and Southampton will square off at Bramall Lane on Tuesday.
  • Both teams got back to winning ways in their first game after the international break on Saturday, leaving the hosts ninth and their visitors sixth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:15.

Separated by just two points in the battle for top-eight places in the Championship table, Sheffield United and Southampton will square off at Bramall Lane on Tuesday.

Both teams got back to winning ways in their first game after the international break on Saturday, leaving the hosts ninth and their visitors sixth.

Sheffield United return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back home wins and break into the Championship playoff places.

Aiming to build on 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a Premier League return, the Blades have experienced a mixed start to the season but enjoyed a positive run after the first international break of the campaign, winning four and drawing one of their first six matches October and November, only to go into the November break following a 2-1 away defeat to Charlton Athletic.

That cost the Chris Wilder's side a place in the playoff spots in the second international break of the season, having returned at home to Watford on Saturday with 22 points on the board from their first 15 matches.

The Blades again returned to winning ways in that contest at Bramall Lane, dishing out a 4-0 beating as Ben Brereton Diaz scored a brace inside 20 minutes, Jordan Ayew stretched the lead on the hour mark and Sydie Peck scored a fourth in the 84th minute.

Now sat ninth and just two points behind three teams in the top eight including Saturday's visitors, Sheffield United face another test at Bramall Lane with the hopes of cracking the top eight with a second straight triumph and a third straight home victory.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors make the long trip north aiming to strengthen their own standing at the top end of the division and increase pressure on the top two with their own second consecutive win.

After only being denied a place in last season's Championship playoff final by the Spygate scandal last season, which also brought about a two-point deduction this term, Southampton have again enjoyed a strong start to the upcoming term, amassing 29 points from their first 16 matches to sit sixth on 27 points after the deduction.

The Saints have won nine and only lost three of those games, while scoring 31 goals and conceding just 15 - the joint-fewest in the division.

Tonda Eckert's side headed into the November international break on the back of a draw against West Bromwich Albion and a shock defeat to basement team Preston North End, but they bounced back on their return on Saturday, beating Derby County 2-0 thanks to second-half goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.

That leaves Southampton sixth after 16 matches despite their deduction, two points off fourth spot and five off the top two, and they will look to make it consecutive triumphs in Tuesday's trip to Bramall Lane.

Sheffield United Championship form:.

Sheffield United will remain without Femi Seriki, Matt Doherty, Joe Rothwell and Ryan One due to ongoing injuries, while Kalvin Phillips missed out with a minor problem at the weekend and may be in contention to return on Tuesday.

They are unable to go unchanged from Saturday's 4-0 win, with attacker Brereton Diaz unable to feature against his parent club while centre-back and captain Japhet Tanganga is suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards.

In his absence, Mark McGuinness will come in to join Liam Kitching at the back, while Patrick Bamford, Tyrese Campbell, Tom Cannon and Jordan Ayew will compete for two attacking spots.

Southampton will head to Bramall Lane without defender Keven Schlotterbeck and midfielder Casper Jander, both of whom are confined to the treatment room, with the former being forced off early in their defeat to Preston before the break.

The Saints could be unchanged from their win at the weekend, with Zach Abbott having deputised at the back in Schlotterbeck's absence, while Leo Scienza also missed out.

Star forward Larin returned to the starting XI on Saturday and scored to make it eight goals in 12 league appearances this season, while Tom Fellows, Finn Azaz and Samuel Edozie will hope to continue in support of the front man despite competition from Kuryu Matsuki, Lewis Dobbin and Divin Mubama.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:.

Cooper; Choudhury, McGuinness, Kitching, Burrows; Chong, Arblaster, Peck, Donovan; Ayew, Bamford.

Southampton possible starting lineup:.

Peretz; Bree, Stephens, Abbott, Manning; Ward-Prowse, Bragg; Fellows, Azaz, Dobbin; Larin.

Southampton face a tough test in their bid to further ramp up their pursuit of the top two, having fought from behind this season, on Tuesday.

While they boast more quality than the hosts, Sheffield United certainly appear to be growing into the campaign, and we anticipate a share of the points at Bramall Lane.

Industry observers note that switching several key players after the international break was a brave move designed to revitalise West Ham’s fortunes. Had the ball not crashed against the woodwork four times but nestled in the corner just once we’d all be proclaiming his changes as astute: Bringing back Alvarez and switching Morato to a centre back role weren’t rocket science but shored up a hitherto leaky defence.

However, bringing Fin Herrick into the side – ostensibly ‘resting’ (a.k.a.’dropping’) Hermansen – paid off . With Herrick now tried and tested, his elevation to credible first team keeper surely puts paid to any interest West Ham were showing in young Swansea ‘keeper Joe Duncan.

Herrick’s emergence means the budget doesn’t have to be diluted: Koppen can call off the search for a ‘keeper and find a goal scorer instead.

A sterner test will come at Portsmouth but saving Koppen’s transfer budget for the acquisition of a striker who can actually hit the target looks to be the 100% absolute stone-cold priority in January, if it isn’t already too late.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.
  • Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history.
  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

It has been revealed that A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

In a recent development, he was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Sources indicate that storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

In a recent development, storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

The 47-year-old remarked: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park.

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

'Today they did it and hopefully they felt it can work and they can show it more.

'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

It has been revealed that 'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'.

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

He noted: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and highlights grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

'I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scott Parker’s decision to recall Soungoutou Magassa from the ‘Nuno wilderness’ back into the West Ham fold looks well founded.

Similarly, the apparent re-integration of Edson Alvarez into West Ham United’s starting eleven last weekend has been met with almost universal approval after the Mexican’s decent showing against Preston.

At the very least, these two players will see their transfer values rise simply by being deployed in competitive football. At best, they could contribute significantly towards a successful outcome for the club this season.

All of which makes Niclas Fullkrug’s escapades in Germany even more ironic, as West Ham’s failure to score their winner after thirty attempts gets put into sharp relief by their on-loan striker becoming the Bundesliga’s top scorer.

In a recent development, another goal by Fullkrug at the weekend in Bremen’s 4- 0 victory will make Hammers fans scratch their head and wonder whether, with different coaching and different attitudes, the German could have made an impact in east London this season. He’d certainly have got some game time.

Fullkrug is now the top scorer in the German league after his ninth goal for Werder Bremen at the weekend.

Too late to think about recalling Fullkrug, it seems he’s found his spiritual ‘home’, and good luck to him.

It does throw the coaching failures of the last three of West Ham’s so called ‘managers’ sharply into focus when they all relied heavily on their favourites and ‘fell out’ frequently with players: Who can forget Lopetegui’s dressing room bust-ups with Mohammed Kudus and Jean-Clair Todibo?

Eye-watering sums are spent by football clubs on researching, scouting and recruiting players, but then whole careers seem ended on a managerial whim or a clash of egos.

By no means unique to West Ham, but it is an area in which clubs have to learn to do better or risk losing, as in Fullkrug’s case, the very stars who can fire the goals they’ve just paid through the nose to acquire.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:35.

In search of a third straight victory with the chance to further narrow their gap to the top two in the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will head to the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday to take on Stevenage.

The visitors have moved to fifth spot and three points behind the automatic promotion places under newly introduced management while their hosts sit 14th following a return to winning ways at the weekend.

Stevenage return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back victories and finally kickstart their League One season.

After a memorable campaign last time around ended in a sixth-placed finish against the odds on 75 points and eventual playoff defeat, they are yet to truly get going and build on that in 2025-26, having headed into last weekend following the international break on 16 points from 12 league matches.

The last of those matches was a creditable draw against Leicester City, though, before Alex Revell's men recorded consecutive cup victories over Oxford United and Fulham Under-21s and returned to action away at Notts County last weekend.

The Boro would put a fifth three-point haul of the campaign on the board in that contest, as it looked set to end goalless only for Josh Magennis to break the deadlock four minutes from time.

Now sat 14th on 19 points, but just four points off the playoff spots with at least one game in hand on every team above them, Stevenage do have the chance to put themselves in a strong position if they can build on Saturday's win in the next few outings.

That will be no easy task, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue a perfect start to life under fresh management in the league.

Sheffield Wednesday arrived in League One, albeit on the back of relegation and administration last time around, with fresh optimism, a fresh-look squad and ownership and hopes to bounce back to the second tier at the first time of asking, and after a fast start, manager Henrik Pedersen's tenure would end with consecutive defeats to Notts County and Doncaster Rovers.

A pair of draws followed before the club hierarchy turned to Dave Challinor, whose tenure begun with back-to-back cup defeats to Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley.

It is clear their priorities lie with the league, though, and he has overseen victories in his first two third-tier matches at the helm, as the Owls firstly beat fellow promotion-chasers Plymouth Argyle 3-0 at Hillsborough before visiting Barnsley in a South Yorkshire Derby on Friday and winning 2-1 thanks to Jamal Lowe's first-half brace.

That leaves them fifth with momentum back on their side and just a three-point gap to second spot, and Sheffield Wednesday will now bid to make it three wins in three League One games under Challinor to further ramp up the pressure on the automatic promotion places.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Sheffield Wednesday League One form:.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):.

Stevenage will remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts on Tuesday due to ongoing injuries.

Revell should field a similar starting XI from the weekend's away win, although Magennis will likely return from the outset having won that game off the bench with his fourth League One goal of the season having also recorded four assists as their focal point.

He could be joined in a front two by Michael Mellon, who has seven goals in all competitions in the absence of supporting midfielder Kemp, while Louis Thompson and Daniel Phillips will continue their midfield partnership having been regulars this term after several major departures for the Boro over the summer.

Sheffield Wednesday could be unchanged from their victory on Friday, with Reece James, Max Lowe, Tyler Onyango, Mason Burstow and Ali Al-Hamadi likely to miss out again through injury.

Their injury troubles have eased recently, though, with Joe Lumley, Liam Cooper, Di'Shon Bernard, Billy Mitchell and Louie Barry all available after layoffs, and Cooper and Bernard will continue to play in a back three.

The absence of Lowe and James leaves a gap at left wing-back, while forward Jamal Lowe has filled in recent games, netting a brace on Friday, while Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery should again support front man Davis Keillor-Dunn with Barry continuing to be eased back after a lengthy spell in the treatment room.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; James-Wildin, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Sanderson, Thompson, Phillips, Patterson; Mellon, Magennis.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels, Valery, Heskey, Mitchell, J Lowe; Slattery, Bannan; Keillor-Dunn.

Stevenage head into Tuesday's game in better shape than their league position suggests and are always difficult to beat, having only conceded 13 league goals this term.

Sheffield Wednesday are growing into life under Challinor, though, and are beginning to show the quality that their squad is packed with, particularly with several key players back to full fitness, and we fancy them to make it three straight wins in a hard-fought away trip.
